stored_metadata.title: Where the species separate
stored_metadata.body: Flipper length and body mass separate *Gentoo* cleanly; *Adelie* and *Chinstrap* overlap on both and only pull apart on bill length. The scatter carries species as colour and island as symbol, so the confound is visible: every *Gentoo* is from Biscoe, every *Chinstrap* from Dream.

stored_metadata.title: Body Mass Distribution by Species

dc_config.description: Complete penguin dataset with physical features and demographics

stored_metadata.description: Violin with the box and every observation inside. Reads against the Body Mass card above: the card's single number is this chart with the species collapsed together. Gentoo's outline is visibly two-humped, which is the male / female split.
stored_metadata.code_content:
fig = px.violin(
    df.to_pandas(),
    x='species', y='body_mass_g', color='species',
    box=True, points='all',
    color_discrete_map={'Adelie': '#FF8C00', 'Chinstrap': '#A034F0', 'Gentoo': '#159090'},
    labels={'body_mass_g': 'Body Mass (g)', 'species': 'Species'},
)
fig.update_traces(meanline_visible=True, marker=dict(size=4, opacity=0.55))

stored_metadata.title: How the cohort is distributed
stored_metadata.body: Torgersen holds *Adelie* only, Biscoe holds *Adelie* and *Gentoo*, Dream holds *Adelie* and *Chinstrap* — *Adelie* is the one species sampled everywhere. Sampling is near-flat across the three seasons (109 / 114 / 119 birds), so a difference between years is unlikely to be an effort artefact.
